docs.title: SystemForge Web
docs.text: React framework for building multi-tenant SaaS applications with SystemForge.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SystemForge Web provides a complete set of React packages for building production-ready SaaS applications:

  • Authentication - Secure BFF-based auth with HTTP-only cookies
  • Multi-tenancy - Organization switching, role-based access
  • Application Shell - Responsive layout with navigation
  • Telemetry - Event tracking and error boundaries
  • Design Tokens - Consistent styling primitives

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package Description @plexusone/auth Authentication primitives (AuthProvider, ProtectedRoute) @plexusone/tenant Multi-tenant context (TenantProvider, RequireRole) @plexusone/api-client HTTP client with auth integration @plexusone/telemetry Event instrumentation and error tracking @plexusone/shell Application shell components @plexusone/pages Pre-built pages (Login, Settings, Error) @plexusone/design-tokens Design system tokens

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import { AuthProvider } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { TenantProvider } from '@plexusone/tenant';
import { AppShell } from '@plexusone/shell';

function App() {
  return (
    <AuthProvider>
      <TenantProvider>
        <AppShell
          brandName="My App"
          navigation={[
            { label: 'Dashboard', href: '/', icon: HomeIcon },
            { label: 'Settings', href: '/settings', icon: SettingsIcon },
          ]}
        >
          <YourRoutes />
        </AppShell>
      </TenantProvider>
    </AuthProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: Composing applications
docs.text:
A SystemForge deployment usually runs more than one application: an identity service, and the products people sign in to. The shell gives them one chrome (a product switcher, an organization switcher and a profile menu) in either of two ways of composing them.

One build One host per application Applications Registered into one front end Each built and deployed on its own host Moving between applications Client-side route change A link to the other host; a full page load Product switcher entries The deployment's app catalog The deployment's app catalog Session One BFF session One BFF session per host, one sign-in through the shared identity service

Both read the same session from the relying-party BFF (GET /bff/session): the person, their memberships keyed by organization ID with the role they hold in each application, and the deployment's app catalog. The product switcher shows the applications the person holds a role in for the current organization, with the current application first.

docs.title: One host per application
docs.text:
Each application wraps itself in SessionProvider and renders the switchers. Links in the product switcher go to each application's host; the person is already signed in through the identity service, so the other application starts its own BFF session without a prompt.

import { SessionProvider } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { OrganizationSwitcher, ProductSwitcher } from '@plexusone/shell';
import { useNavigate, useParams } from 'react-router-dom';

const self = { id: 'reports', name: 'Reports', url: '/' };

function TopBar() {
  const { org } = useParams(); // the organization ID is in the URL
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <header className="flex items-center gap-4 px-4 h-14 border-b border-border">
      <ProductSwitcher self={self} organizationId={org} />
      <OrganizationSwitcher value={org} onChange={(id) => navigate(`/orgs/${id}`)} />
    </header>
  );
}

export function App() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider onUnauthorized={() => window.location.assign('/bff/auth/login')}>
      {/* routes under /orgs/:org render <TopBar /> */}
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: One build
docs.text:
Several applications share one front end and one session. Pass onNavigate so switching products is a route change instead of a page load. The catalog's URLs are then paths within the build.

function TopBar({ current }: { current: { id: string; name: string; url: string } }) {
  const { org } = useParams();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <header className="flex items-center gap-4 px-4 h-14 border-b border-border">
      <ProductSwitcher self={current} organizationId={org} onNavigate={(url) => navigate(url)} />
      <OrganizationSwitcher value={org} onChange={(id) => navigate(`/orgs/${id}`)} />
    </header>
  );
}

docs.title: Rules both modes follow
docs.text:
• The organization is identified by ID, in the URL and in API paths. A slug is for display only.
  • The application owns the current organization. OrganizationSwitcher reports the chosen ID and keeps no state; the application navigates.
  • Roles in the interface only hide things. The product switcher hides applications the person holds no role in, but each application's API enforces its own permissions.
  • Sign-in is a redirect to the BFF. No credentials pass through the shell.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: SystemForge Web follows a modular, composable architecture designed for multi-tenant SaaS applications.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Security First - BFF pattern with HTTP-only cookies, no tokens in localStorage
  2. Composable - Use only the packages you need
  3. Type Safe - Full TypeScript with strict types
  4. Framework Agnostic - Works with any React framework
  5. Backend Agnostic - Works with any backend supporting BFF pattern

docs.title: Provider Hierarchy
docs.text:
The recommended provider order:

<QueryClientProvider>
  {' '}
  {/* TanStack Query */}
  <BrowserRouter>
    {' '}
    {/* React Router */}
    <TelemetryProvider>
      {' '}
      {/* Event tracking */}
      <ErrorBoundary>
        {' '}
        {/* Error handling */}
        <AuthProvider>
          {' '}
          {/* Authentication */}
          <ApiProvider>
            {' '}
            {/* HTTP client */}
            <TenantProvider>
              {' '}
              {/* Multi-tenancy */}
              <AppShell>
                {' '}
                {/* Layout */}
                <App />
              </AppShell>
            </TenantProvider>
          </ApiProvider>
        </AuthProvider>
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </TelemetryProvider>
  </BrowserRouter>
</QueryClientProvider>

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User Action → Component calls hook (e.g., useAuth().login())
  2. Hook → Calls API client method
  3. API Client → Makes HTTP request with cookies
  4. BFF Proxy → Extracts session, forwards with JWT
  5. Backend → Processes request, returns response
  6. Response → Flows back through layers
  7. State Update → React Query cache updated
  8. Re-render → UI reflects new state

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up a basic SystemForge Web application.

docs.title: 1. Create a New Project
docs.text:
pnpm create vite my-app --template react-ts
cd my-app
pnpm install

docs.title: 2. Install SystemForge Web
docs.text:
pnpm add @plexusone/auth @plexusone/tenant @plexusone/shell @plexusone/api-client
pnpm add @tanstack/react-query react-router-dom

docs.title: 3. Set Up Providers
docs.text:
Create src/App.tsx:

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { AuthProvider } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { TenantProvider } from '@plexusone/tenant';
import { ApiProvider } from '@plexusone/api-client';
import { AppShell } from '@plexusone/shell';
import { Routes } from './Routes';

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

export function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <BrowserRouter>
        <AuthProvider bffBaseUrl="/api/auth">
          <ApiProvider baseUrl="/api">
            <TenantProvider>
              <AppShell
                brandName="My App"
                navigation={[
                  { label: 'Dashboard', href: '/' },
                  { label: 'Settings', href: '/settings' },
                ]}
              >
                <Routes />
              </AppShell>
            </TenantProvider>
          </ApiProvider>
        </AuthProvider>
      </BrowserRouter>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: 4. Create Routes
docs.text:
Create src/Routes.tsx:

import { Routes as RouterRoutes, Route } from 'react-router-dom';
import { ProtectedRoute } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { LoginPage } from '@plexusone/pages';

function Dashboard() {
  return <h1>Dashboard</h1>;
}

function Settings() {
  return <h1>Settings</h1>;
}

export function Routes() {
  return (
    <RouterRoutes>
      <Route path="/login" element={<LoginPage />} />
      <Route element={<ProtectedRoute />}>
        <Route path="/" element={<Dashboard />} />
        <Route path="/settings" element={<Settings />} />
      </Route>
    </RouterRoutes>
  );
}

docs.title: 5. Configure Backend Proxy
docs.text:
For development, configure your Vite dev server to proxy API requests:

// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  server: {
    proxy: {
      '/api': {
        target: 'http://localhost:8080',
        changeOrigin: true,
      },
    },
  },
});

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: For maintainers. Packages are versioned by hand and published to npm by hand with pnpm, one package at a time. The release workflow in GitHub Actions does not publish; it runs only when started by hand.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
• The repository is tagged vX.Y.Z for each release. Release notes and the changelog are per repository.
  • Packages are versioned independently. Bump only the packages that changed; a release can move @plexusone/shell to 0.2.3 while the others stay at 0.2.1. Internal ranges are workspace:^, which pnpm publishes as a caret range on the version in the workspace.
  • While the major version is 0, a change a consumer must react to is a new minor version; fixes are patch versions.
  • A published version cannot be replaced. Fix forward with a new version, and deprecate the broken one.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the release
docs.text:
1. Set version in each changed package's package.json.
  2. Add the release to CHANGELOG.json with each change's commit, then generate the changelog:
schangelog validate CHANGELOG.json
schangelog generate CHANGELOG.json -o CHANGELOG.md
cp CHANGELOG.md docs/changelog.md
  1. Add docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md and list it in mkdocs.yml.
  2. Check locally what CI checks:
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build          # ends by loading every package entry point
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm format:check

pnpm build runs scripts/check-exports.mjs, which imports and requires every entry point each package exports. It fails when an export names a file the build does not write, which once shipped a @plexusone/ui that could not load.

docs.title: 2. Push, then tag
docs.text:
1. Push main and wait for CI to pass.
  2. Tag the commit CI passed on, and push the tag:
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z

docs.title: 3. Publish
docs.text:
Publish from main at the tagged commit. pnpm publish refuses a detached HEAD (ERR_PNPM_GIT_UNKNOWN_BRANCH), so check out main, not the tag:

git checkout main
git pull --ff-only
git rev-parse --short HEAD    # must be the tagged commit
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build

Sign in, then publish each changed package with its own command, in dependency order: ui and auth before tenant, and all three before shell; auth before pages.

npm login
npm whoami                    # grokify
pnpm --filter @plexusone/ui publish --access public
pnpm --filter @plexusone/auth publish --access public
pnpm --filter @plexusone/tenant publish --access public
pnpm --filter @plexusone/shell publish --access public

Do not use pnpm -r publish. It decides what to publish by asking the registry, which can lag behind a version just published or staged; it then publishes that version again, npm answers E409 Cannot publish over previously staged version, and the run stops before the remaining packages.

docs.title: A new package goes through staging
docs.text: The first version of a package that is not yet on npm is staged: npm publishes a public 0.0.0-stage placeholder and holds the real version until a maintainer approves it. Approve it in Staged Packages on npmjs.com, with two-factor authentication, before publishing a package that depends on it. With npm 11.15 or later, npm stage list and npm stage approve <id> do the same from the terminal.

docs.title: When publishing fails
docs.text: Error Cause What to do ERR_PNPM_GIT_UNKNOWN_BRANCH HEAD is detached, as after checking out a tag Check out main at the tagged commit E404 on PUT Not signed in, or the token expired (sign-in tokens are short-lived) npm login, then npm whoami E409 Cannot publish over previously staged version That version is already published or staged Skip it; publish the next package E402 Publishing a scoped package as restricted Every package sets publishConfig.access: public; pass --access public

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
The registry can take a minute to show a new version. Then install the published packages into an empty project and load them, which is what a consumer does:

mkdir /tmp/check && cd /tmp/check && npm init -y >/dev/null
npm install react@19 react-dom@19 @plexusone/shell @plexusone/auth @plexusone/tenant @plexusone/ui
node --input-type=module -e "await import('@plexusone/shell'); console.log('import ok')"
node -e "require('@plexusone/shell'); console.log('require ok')"

If a published version is broken, publish a fixed version and deprecate the broken one:

npm deprecate @plexusone/ui@0.2.1 "broken exports; use 0.2.2"

docs.title: @plexusone/api-client
docs.text: HTTP client with authentication and tenant context integration.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pnpm add @plexusone/api-client @tanstack/react-query

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Automatic authentication headers
  • Tenant context injection
  • TanStack Query integration
  • Request/response interceptors
  • TypeScript-first API

docs.title: ApiProvider
docs.text:
Wrap your application with ApiProvider:

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ApiProvider } from '@plexusone/api-client';

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <AuthProvider>
        <ApiProvider baseUrl="/api">
          <YourApp />
        </ApiProvider>
      </AuthProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: useApi Hook
docs.text:
Make API calls with automatic auth:

import { useApi } from '@plexusone/api-client';

function UserList() {
  const api = useApi();

  const { data, isLoading } = api.useQuery(['users'], '/users');

  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>;

  return (
    <ul>
      {data.map((user) => (
        <li key={user.id}>{user.name}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text:
import { useApi } from '@plexusone/api-client';

function CreateUser() {
  const api = useApi();

  const mutation = api.useMutation('/users', {
    method: 'POST',
    onSuccess: () => {
      // Handle success
    },
  });

  const handleSubmit = (data: CreateUserData) => {
    mutation.mutate(data);
  };

  return <UserForm onSubmit={handleSubmit} isLoading={mutation.isPending} />;
}

docs.title: Direct Client Access
docs.text:
import { useApiClient } from '@plexusone/api-client';

function DownloadReport() {
  const client = useApiClient();

  const download = async () => {
    const response = await client.get('/reports/download', {
      responseType: 'blob',
    });
    // Handle blob response
  };

  return <button onClick={download}>Download</button>;
}

docs.text:
Access authentication state and methods:

import { useAuth } from '@plexusone/auth';

function UserInfo() {
  const { user, isAuthenticated, isLoading, login, logout } = useAuth();

  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>;

  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return <button onClick={() => login()}>Login</button>;
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Welcome, {user.name}</p>
      <button onClick={() => logout()}>Logout</button>

    <Routes>
      <Route path="/login" element={<LoginPage />} />

docs.title: Linked Accounts
docs.text:
Manage OAuth provider connections:

import { useLinkedAccounts } from '@plexusone/auth';

function LinkedAccounts() {
  const { accounts, link, unlink } = useLinkedAccounts();

  return (
    <div>
      {accounts.map((account) => (
        <div key={account.provider}>
          {account.provider}: {account.connected ? 'Connected' : 'Not connected'}
          <button
            onClick={() => (account.connected ? unlink(account.provider) : link(account.provider))}
          >
            {account.connected ? 'Disconnect' : 'Connect'}
          </button>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: Session over the BFF
docs.text:
SessionProvider reads GET /bff/session from the relying-party BFF and useSession returns it: the person, their memberships keyed by organization ID with a role per application, and the deployment's app catalog. Sign-in is a redirect; sign-out is a same-origin POST.

import { SessionProvider, useSession, membershipFor } from '@plexusone/auth';

function Who({ org }: { org: string }) {
  const { status, session, signIn, signOut } = useSession();
  if (status === 'loading') return null;
  if (status !== 'authenticated') return <button onClick={() => signIn()}>Sign in</button>;
  const role = membershipFor(session, org)?.applications['reports'];
  return (
    <span>
      {session.user?.name} ({role ?? 'no role'}){' '}
      <button onClick={() => void signOut()}>Sign out</button>
    </span>
  );
}

<SessionProvider onUnauthorized={() => window.location.assign('/bff/auth/login')}>
  <Who org={orgId} />
</SessionProvider>;

The session is re-read when the window regains focus and every five minutes (refreshInterval, refreshOnFocus). onUnauthorized runs when a signed-in session is found signed out, not after a deliberate sign-out.

docs.text:
ProductSwitcher lists the deployment's applications the person holds a role in for the current organization, from the session's app catalog, with the current application first. OrganizationSwitcher is controlled: it reports the chosen organization's ID and the application navigates. Both read the session from SessionProvider in @plexusone/auth. See Composing applications.

<ProductSwitcher self={{ id: 'reports', name: 'Reports', url: '/' }} organizationId={org} />
<OrganizationSwitcher value={org} onChange={(id) => navigate(`/orgs/${id}`)} />

OrgSwitcher remains for applications that keep the current organization in TenantProvider.

docs.title: Profile menu
docs.text:
Under SessionProvider, the bar shows ProfileMenu: who is signed in, the current organization, the role held in this application (falling back to the organization role), the application's profileItems, and sign out. It has no default links. Applications on AuthProvider keep UserMenu, whose default links were removed for the same reason.

<AppShell
  appName="Reports"
  app={{ id: 'reports', name: 'Reports', url: '/' }}
  organizationId={org}
  onOrganizationChange={(id) => navigate(`/orgs/${id}`)}
  profileItems={[{ id: 'keys', label: 'API keys', href: `/orgs/${org}/keys` }]}
>
  {children}
</AppShell>

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
showThemeToggle adds a toggle that cycles light, dark and the system's preference. The choice is stored in local storage and applied as the dark class on the root element, which the design system's styles key on; while on system it follows the operating system's preference as it changes. If storage is unavailable the choice lasts for the page.

Call applyStoredTheme() before the first render so the page does not flash the other theme:

import { applyStoredTheme } from '@plexusone/shell';

applyStoredTheme();
createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);

useTheme() returns the choice and a setter for an application that renders its own control.

docs.text:

import { JourneyProvider, useJourneyStep } from '@plexusone/telemetry';

function App() {
  return (
    <JourneyProvider journeyId="checkout_flow">
      <CheckoutWizard />
    </JourneyProvider>
  );
}

function PaymentStep() {
  const { enterStep, completeStep, abandonStep } = useJourneyStep(
    'payment',
    'Enter Payment Details'
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    enterStep();
    return () => completeStep();
  }, []);

  return <PaymentForm />;
}

docs.title: State Change Tracking
docs.text:
Track state changes with before/after values:

import { useStateTracker } from '@plexusone/telemetry';

function CartPage() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState([]);

  // Tracks changes to cart.items with before/after values
  useStateTracker('cart.items', items, {
    debounce: 500, // Debounce rapid changes
  });

  return <CartList items={items} />;
}

docs.title: Component Path Tracking
docs.text:
Build component hierarchy for debugging:

import { ComponentPathProvider, useComponentPath } from '@plexusone/telemetry';

function App() {
  return (
    <ComponentPathProvider name="App">
      <Dashboard />
    </ComponentPathProvider>
  );
}

function Widget() {
  const path = useComponentPath();
  // path = ['App', 'Dashboard', 'Widget']

  return <div>...</div>;
}

docs.title: @plexusone/tenant
docs.text: Multi-tenancy primitives for organization-based applications.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pnpm add @plexusone/tenant

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Organization context management
  • Organization switching
  • Role-based access control
  • Membership management
  • TypeScript-first API

docs.title: TenantProvider
docs.text:
Wrap your application with TenantProvider (inside AuthProvider):

import { AuthProvider } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { TenantProvider } from '@plexusone/tenant';

function App() {
  return (
    <AuthProvider bffBaseUrl="/api/auth">
      <TenantProvider>
        <YourApp />
      </TenantProvider>
    </AuthProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: useOrganization Hook
docs.text:
Access the current organization:

import { useOrganization } from '@plexusone/tenant';

function OrgInfo() {
  const { organization, membership, isLoading } = useOrganization();

  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>;

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>{organization.name}</h2>
      <p>Your role: {membership.role}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: useOrganizations Hook
docs.text:
List and switch organizations:

import { useOrganizations } from '@plexusone/tenant';

function OrgSwitcher() {
  const { organizations, currentOrg, switchOrg, isLoading } = useOrganizations();

  return (
    <select value={currentOrg?.id} onChange={(e) => switchOrg(e.target.value)} disabled={isLoading}>
      {organizations.map((org) => (
        <option key={org.id} value={org.id}>
          {org.name}
        </option>
      ))}
    </select>
  );
}

docs.title: RequireRole
docs.text:
Restrict access based on role:

import { RequireRole } from '@plexusone/tenant';

function AdminPanel() {
  return (
    <RequireRole roles={['admin', 'owner']} fallback={<AccessDenied />}>
      <AdminDashboard />
    </RequireRole>
  );
}

Styles
docs.text:
The package publishes two things for styling:

  • @plexusone/ui/globals.css: compiled CSS with the theme's values (the --color-* variables, light and .dark) and the classes these components use.
  • @plexusone/ui/tailwind: a Tailwind config that gives the theme's colors names (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, border-border).

import { TelemetryProvider, ProductGraphAdapter } from '@systemforge/telemetry';

const adapter = new ProductGraphAdapter({
  projectId: 'my-project',

docs.title: v0.2.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-10-15

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A session from the relying-party BFF. @plexusone/auth adds SessionProvider and useSession, which read /bff/session: the person, their memberships keyed by organization ID with a role per application, and the deployment's app catalog.
  • Shell chrome for composed applications. @plexusone/shell adds a product switcher from the app catalog, a controlled organization switcher, a session profile menu, named slots for an application's own controls, and a light, dark and system theme.
  • Organization management pages in @plexusone/pages, and @plexusone/chat with AI SDK integration.
  • Published as @plexusone/*, publicly, on React 19.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
1. Scope and React. Import from @plexusone/* instead of @systemforge/*, and use React 19.
  2. UserMenu has no default links. It no longer adds Profile and Settings entries pointing at /settings/profile and /settings. Pass them in userActions to keep them.
  3. Applications on a SystemForge relying party can drop their own top bar:
<SessionProvider>
  <AppShell
    appName="Reports"
    app={{ id: 'reports', name: 'Reports', url: '/' }}
    organizationId={org}
    onOrganizationChange={(id) => navigate(`/orgs/${id}`)}
    showThemeToggle
  >
    {routes}
  </AppShell>
</SessionProvider>

See Composing applications.

Piece What it does ProductSwitcher The current application first, then the catalog applications the person holds a role in for the current organization; links across hosts, or onNavigate in one build OrganizationSwitcher Controlled, keyed by organization ID; reports the chosen ID and keeps no state ProfileMenu Who is signed in, the current organization and the role in this application, profileItems, sign out Slots brand, command and actions on Navbar and AppShell Theme showThemeToggle, useTheme and applyStoredTheme; the dark class on the root element, surviving unavailable storage

docs.title: PLAN — Shell Foundations — Session, App Catalog, Organizations and Slots for Composed Apps
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGEWEB-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemforge-web

docs.title: Approach
docs.text: Build from the data up: the session model first, because the switchers, the profile menu and the brand all read from it. Then the chrome, then the brand and baseline that let a deployment adopt the shell without forking it. Each phase is releasable, and existing exports keep working throughout.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Session and Switching
docs.text:
1. Add the session types and an adapter from the BFF's /bff/session JSON, with fixtures for the cases in the TRD.
  2. Add SessionProvider and useSession, with redirect sign-in, sign-out, refresh on focus and an onUnauthorized hook.
  3. Add switcherApps as a pure function with tests, then the ProductSwitcher component.
  4. Make OrgSwitcher controllable by value and onChange, keyed by organization ID, and keep the current behavior behind an opt-in.
  5. Write the composition modes guide and two examples.

Exit: an example application on one host and an example with two registered applications both render the switchers from a fixture session.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Chrome
docs.text:
1. Add the slots to Navbar and AppShell, keeping current props as defaults.
  2. Add the theme toggle and its storage fallback.
  3. Rework UserMenu into the profile menu: empty default actions, organization and role rows, profileItems.
  4. Apply the ui tooltip to icon-only controls and add keyboard and focus tests.
  5. Add the responsive collapse and the navigation model option.

Exit: an application needs no top-bar code of its own; the component tests cover keyboard use and focus.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Brand and Baseline
docs.text:
1. Define BrandConfig and apply tokens through @plexusone/design-tokens.
  2. Decide styling delivery in an ADR and ship compiled CSS.
  3. Publish TypeScript, lint and test presets.
  4. Release, with migration notes for the changed UserMenu defaults and the new organization switcher mode.

Exit: a deployment's brand package changes the look with no shell fork, and the release notes cover every behavior change.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Vitest and Testing Library at the workspace root. Every RMI adds or updates tests in the package it changes; the session fixtures are shared.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• The relying-party BFF's /bff/session response, as served by SystemForge.
  • INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-001 Phase 3 builds its registration contract and reference host on this initiative's session, switchers and slots.

docs.title: PRD — Shell Foundations — Session, App Catalog, Organizations and Slots for Composed Apps
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGEWEB-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemforge-web Related: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-001 (Phase 3, Shell Composition)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: @plexusone/shell should be the one chrome every SystemForge application uses: the top bar, the product switcher, the organization switcher, the profile menu and the places an application puts its own controls. Today the package has the pieces (AppShell, Navbar, OrgSwitcher, UserMenu, Breadcrumbs) but none of the data model SystemForge's relying party actually serves, so applications built on SystemForge write their own top bars instead. This initiative closes that gap.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
• Applications copy the chrome. Each application on a SystemForge deployment builds its own top bar, product switcher and profile menu. They drift in behavior (how the switcher filters, how switching organization works) and in look, and a fix has to be made once per application.
  • The shell speaks a different session. @plexusone/auth targets email-and-password routes and a user with one role per membership. The relying-party BFF serves /bff/session: the user, memberships with a role per application, and the deployment's application catalog. The shell cannot see per-application roles or the catalog.
  • Organization switching does not fit. The shell keeps the current organization in local storage. SystemForge applications put the organization in the URL and in API paths, keyed by organization ID.
  • No place for an application's own controls. Search, notifications or a product's action menu can only be added by forking the navbar.
  • Two composition modes, one shell. Some deployments build several applications into one front end (the Forge composition of INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-001). Others serve each application from its own host and link them through the app catalog. The shell has to serve both.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: User Needs Application developer Drop in the shell, pass the application's identity and slots, and get sign-in, switching and the profile menu working against SystemForge Deployment operator Applications that look and behave as one product, with the catalog deciding what appears End user One consistent way to move between products and organizations, see who is signed in, and sign out

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. A session model over the relying-party BFF, exposing memberships with per-application roles and the app catalog.
  2. A product switcher built from the catalog that shows only the applications the person holds a role in for the current organization, with the current application always first.
  3. An organization switcher that is controlled by the application and keyed by organization ID.
  4. Named slots for an application's own content in the top bar.
  5. Theme, profile menu, tooltips and accessibility handled once.
  6. A brand configuration interface, so a deployment can skin the shell without forking it.
  7. A documented baseline: React version, styling delivery and test setup.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Page content, dashboards or application-specific screens.
  • The ForgeApp registration contract and the reference composed host (RMI-SYSTEMFORGEWEB-002 and -003 in INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-001). This initiative provides what they build on.
  • Customer-embedded mode (embedding one capability into a third-party product).
  • Server changes, beyond what the BFF already serves.

docs.title: Success criteria
docs.text:
• An application renders the full chrome with <AppShell> and its own identity, with no top-bar code of its own.
  • The switcher, organization switcher and profile menu behave the same in every application, covered by the package's tests.
  • A deployment changes its look through brand configuration alone.
  • Both composition modes are documented and covered by an example.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Styling. The shell uses Tailwind classes. Applications that do not use Tailwind need compiled CSS, or adopting the shell means adopting Tailwind.
  • React baseline. The packages require React 19; applications on React 18 must upgrade to adopt the shell.
  • Over-fitting. The session model must follow what the BFF serves, not one deployment's conventions.

All packages declare react ^19.0.0 as a peer dependency.

docs.title: Composition modes
docs.text:
The shell supports two ways of composing applications. Everything in this initiative works in both.

Single build Per host Applications Registered into one front end (ForgeApp, INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-001) Each built and deployed on its own host Moving between applications Client-side route change A link to another host, full page load Product switcher entries Registered applications The deployment's app catalog Session One BFF session One BFF session per host, one sign-in through the shared identity provider

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
A SessionProvider reads /bff/session from the relying-party BFF:

interface Session {
  authenticated: boolean;
  user?: SessionUser;
  apps: CatalogApp[]; // the deployment's application catalog
}
interface SessionUser {
  id: string; // principal ID
  name?: string;
  email?: string;
  avatarUrl?: string;
  memberships: Membership[];
}
interface Membership {
  organizationId: string; // the key; never a slug
  organizationName?: string;
  organizationSlug?: string; // display only
  role?: string; // organization role
  applications: Record<string, string>; // application ID -> role
}
interface CatalogApp {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  url: string;
  icon?: string;
}
  • Field names map from the BFF's JSON in one adapter, so the BFF's wire format does not leak into components.
  • Sign-in redirects to /bff/auth/login?return_to= or a provider route. Sign-out posts to /bff/auth/logout. No credentials pass through the shell.
  • The provider re-reads the session on focus and on an interval, and exposes onUnauthorized so an application can redirect.
  • @plexusone/auth's email-and-password flows stay available for deployments that use them; they are not the default.

docs.title: Product switcher
docs.text:
function switcherApps(apps: CatalogApp[], self: CatalogApp, membership?: Membership): CatalogApp[];
  • Shows catalog applications in which the member holds a role for the current organization (membership.applications[app.id]).
  • The current application is always present and first, and marked aria-current="page".
  • With an empty catalog (local development) it shows the current application alone.
  • Entries for other hosts are links. In single-build mode the application can supply onNavigate for client-side routing.

This rule is a pure function with unit tests, and the component renders it.

docs.title: Organization switcher
docs.text:
• Controlled: value (organization ID) and onChange(organizationId). The application decides how the organization is carried, normally in the URL.
  • Lists the person's memberships by name, falling back to slug, then ID.
  • Hidden with one membership unless alwaysShow is set.
  • @plexusone/tenant's local-storage behavior remains as an opt-in uncontrolled mode.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
AppShell and Navbar accept named slots:

Slot Position Typical content brand Start Overrides the brand from configuration command After the product switcher Search or command bar actions Before the profile menu Product actions, notifications breadcrumbs Below or beside the bar Location within the application profileItems Inside the profile menu Application links

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: SystemForge Web is an open-source React framework providing a complete web application shell with authentication, multi-tenant organization management, and ProductGraph-ready telemetry for applications built on the SystemForge backend platform. It enables rapid development of production-ready multi-tenant SaaS applications with consistent UX patterns.

docs.title: Current Challenges
docs.text:
1. Inconsistent Auth Patterns: App1 uses secure BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) with HTTP-only cookies, while App2 stores tokens in localStorage (XSS vulnerable)
  2. Duplicated Shell Components: Each application reimplements navigation, user menus, organization switchers, and settings pages
  3. No Observability Foundation: Applications lack instrumentation for user journey analytics, making future ProductGraph integration difficult
  4. Design Drift: No shared design system leads to visual inconsistency across the ecosystem
  5. No Account Linking: Users cannot easily switch between linked accounts (like Gmail/HubSpot pattern)

docs.title: Target Applications
docs.text: Application Domain Current State App1-UI Learning Management System React 19, BFF auth, TanStack Query App2-web Professional Credibility React 18, localStorage tokens, Zustand App3 Dashboard Builder React 18, no auth implemented

docs.title: Primary Goals
docs.text:
1. Open Source Web Shell: Complete application shell with navigation, user menu, and multi-tenant support
  2. Unified Secure Authentication: Single BFF-based auth implementation with account linking
  3. Multi-Tenant First: Built-in organization management, role hierarchies, and SaaS admin capabilities
  4. ProductGraph-Ready Instrumentation: Event telemetry hooks integrated throughout the shell
  5. Design System Integration: Tokens and components defined via design-system-spec format

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Domain-specific components (course editors, proof pages, dashboard builders)
  • Backend implementation (SystemForge backend already provides these APIs)
  • Mobile applications (web-first focus)

docs.title: 1. Application Developer
docs.text:
• Builds features on App1, App2, or App3
  • Needs: Ready-to-use shell, quick auth setup, typed API client
  • Pain: Reimplementing navigation, settings, org switching for each app

docs.title: 2. End User (Multi-Account)
docs.text:
• Uses multiple organizations or linked accounts
  • Needs: Quick account switching, unified settings, consistent navigation
  • Pain: Logging out/in to switch contexts, inconsistent UX across apps

docs.title: 3. Organization Admin
docs.text:
• Manages team members and organization settings
  • Needs: Member management, role assignment, org settings
  • Pain: Building admin UIs from scratch for each app

docs.title: 4. SaaS Platform Admin
docs.text:
• Manages the entire platform (non-tenant scope)
  • Needs: Cross-org visibility, platform settings, user management
  • Pain: No standard admin shell for platform-level operations

docs.title: 5. Product Manager
docs.text:
• Analyzes user behavior across applications
  • Needs: User journey data, funnel analytics, engagement metrics
  • Pain: No instrumentation, siloed analytics per app

docs.title: Account Linking & Switching
docs.text:
Similar to Gmail/HubSpot, users can:

  • Link multiple OAuth accounts (GitHub, Google, SystemAuth)
  • Switch between organizations without full logout
  • Switch between linked accounts in one click
  • See all available contexts in a unified menu

// AppShell.tsx

import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
import { TopBar } from './TopBar';
import { LeftNav } from './LeftNav';
import { MobileMenu } from './MobileMenu';
import { UserMenu } from './UserMenu';
import { useInstrumented } from '@plexusone/telemetry';
import type { AppShellProps } from './types';

export function AppShell({
  children,
  logo,
  brandName,
  homeUrl = '/',
  navItems,
  footerNavItems,
  topBarRight,
  leftNavBottom,
  leftNavTop,
  defaultCollapsed = false,
  hideOrgSwitcher = false,
  userMenu,
}: AppShellProps) {
  const [collapsed, setCollapsed] = useState(defaultCollapsed);
  const [mobileMenuOpen, setMobileMenuOpen] = useState(false);

  const { trackClick } = useInstrumented({
    component: 'AppShell',
  });

  const handleNavToggle = useCallback(() => {
    setCollapsed((prev) => !prev);
    trackClick('toggle_nav', 'collapse_button');
  }, [trackClick]);

  const handleMobileMenuToggle = useCallback(() => {
    setMobileMenuOpen((prev) => !prev);
    trackClick('toggle_mobile_menu', 'hamburger');
  }, [trackClick]);

  return (
    <div className="cf-shell">
      <TopBar
        logo={logo}
        brandName={brandName}
        homeUrl={homeUrl}
        rightContent={
          <>
            {topBarRight}
            {userMenu ?? <UserMenu />}
          </>
        }
        onMenuToggle={handleMobileMenuToggle}
        showMenuButton
      />

      <div className="cf-shell-body">
        <LeftNav
          navItems={navItems}
          footerNavItems={footerNavItems}
          topContent={leftNavTop}
          bottomContent={leftNavBottom}
          collapsed={collapsed}
          onCollapsedChange={handleNavToggle}
          hideOrgSwitcher={hideOrgSwitcher}
        />

        <main className="cf-shell-content">
          {children}
        </main>
      </div>

      <MobileMenu
        open={mobileMenuOpen}
        onClose={() => setMobileMenuOpen(false)}
        navItems={navItems}
        footerNavItems={footerNavItems}
        hideOrgSwitcher={hideOrgSwitcher}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

  hideSettings = false,
}: UserMenuProps) {

  const { user, logout } = useAuth();
  const { linkedAccounts, switchAccount } = useLinkedAccounts();
  const { organizations } = useOrganizations();
  const { currentOrg, setCurrentOrg } = useCurrentOrg();

  const { trackClick } = useInstrumented({ component: 'UserMenu' });

  if (!user) return null;

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    trackClick('logout', 'logout_button');
    await logout();
  };

  const handleSwitchAccount = (accountId: string) => {
    trackClick('switch_account', 'account_item', { target_account: accountId });
    switchAccount(accountId);
    setOpen(false);
  };

  const handleSwitchOrg = (orgId: string) => {
    trackClick('switch_org', 'org_item', { target_org: orgId });
    setCurrentOrg(orgId);
    setOpen(false);
  };

  return (
    <div className="cf-user-menu">
      <button
        className="cf-user-menu-trigger"
        onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-haspopup="menu"

          alt={user.name || user.email}

        <span className="cf-user-name">{user.name || user.email}</span>

            <div>
              <div className="cf-user-menu-name">{user.name}</div>
              <div className="cf-user-menu-email">{user.email}</div>
            </div>
          </div>

          {/* Organization switcher */}
          {organizations.length > 1 && (
            <div className="cf-user-menu-section">
              <div className="cf-user-menu-section-title">Organizations</div>
              {organizations.map((org) => (
                <button
                  key={org.id}
                  className="cf-user-menu-item"
                  onClick={() => handleSwitchOrg(org.id)}
                  aria-current={org.id === currentOrg?.id ? 'true' : undefined}
                >
                  {org.name}
                  {org.id === currentOrg?.id && <CheckIcon />}
                </button>
              ))}
            </div>
          )}

          {/* Linked accounts */}
          {!hideLinkedAccounts && linkedAccounts.length > 0 && (
            <div className="cf-user-menu-section">
              <div className="cf-user-menu-section-title">Switch Account</div>
              {linkedAccounts.map((account) => (
                <button
                  key={account.id}
                  className="cf-user-menu-item"
                  onClick={() => handleSwitchAccount(account.id)}
                >
                  <ProviderIcon provider={account.provider} />
                  {account.email}
                </button>
              ))}
            </div>
          )}

          {/* Additional items */}
          {additionalItems?.map((item) => (
            <a key={item.id} href={item.href} className="cf-user-menu-item">
              {item.icon && <item.icon className="cf-icon" />}
              {item.label}
            </a>
          ))}

          {/* Settings */}
          {!hideSettings && (
            <a href="/settings" className="cf-user-menu-item">
              <SettingsIcon className="cf-icon" />

          )}

          {/* Logout */}

}

// TenantProvider.tsx

import { createContext, useContext, useState, useEffect, useCallback, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { useAuth } from '@plexusone/auth';
import { getEmitter } from '@plexusone/telemetry';
import type { Organization, Membership, TenantContextValue } from './types';

const TenantContext = createContext<TenantContextValue | undefined>(undefined);

export interface TenantProviderProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  /** Initial organization ID (from URL or localStorage) */
  initialOrgId?: string;
  /** Storage key for persisting selected org */
  storageKey?: string;
}

export function TenantProvider({
  children,
  initialOrgId,
  storageKey = 'systemforge:current_org',
}: TenantProviderProps) {
  const { user, isAuthenticated } = useAuth();
  const [currentOrgId, setCurrentOrgId] = useState<string | null>(() => {
    return initialOrgId || localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
  });
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);

  // Derive organizations from user memberships
  const organizations: Organization[] = user?.memberships.map((m) => ({
    id: m.organization_id,
    name: m.organization_name,
    slug: m.organization_slug,
    role: m.role,
  })) ?? [];

  // Find current organization
  const currentOrg = organizations.find((o) => o.id === currentOrgId) ?? organizations[0] ?? null;

  // Find current membership
  const currentMembership = user?.memberships.find(
    (m) => m.organization_id === currentOrgId
  ) ?? null;

  // Auto-select first org if none selected
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isAuthenticated && !currentOrgId && organizations.length > 0) {
      setCurrentOrgId(organizations[0].id);
    }
    setIsLoading(false);
  }, [isAuthenticated, currentOrgId, organizations]);

  // Persist org selection
  useEffect(() => {
    if (currentOrgId) {
      localStorage.setItem(storageKey, currentOrgId);
    }
  }, [currentOrgId, storageKey]);

  const setCurrentOrg = useCallback((orgId: string) => {
    const emitter = getEmitter();
    emitter?.emit('custom', {
      action: 'org_switch',
      metadata: {
        from_org_id: currentOrgId,
        to_org_id: orgId,
      },
    });
    setCurrentOrgId(orgId);
  }, [currentOrgId]);

  // Check if user is platform admin (non-tenant scope)
  const isPlatformAdmin = user?.memberships.some(
    (m) => m.role === 'platform_admin'
  ) ?? false;

  return (
    <TenantContext.Provider
      value={{
        organizations,
        currentOrg,
        currentMembership,
        setCurrentOrg,
        isLoading,
        isPlatformAdmin,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </TenantContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useOrganization() {
  const context = useContext(TenantContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useOrganization must be used within TenantProvider');
  }
  return {
    organization: context.currentOrg,
    isLoading: context.isLoading,
  };
}

export function useOrganizations() {
  const context = useContext(TenantContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useOrganizations must be used within TenantProvider');
  }
  return {
    organizations: context.organizations,
    isLoading: context.isLoading,
  };
}

export function useMembership() {
  const context = useContext(TenantContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useMembership must be used within TenantProvider');
  }
  return {
    membership: context.currentMembership,
    isPlatformAdmin: context.isPlatformAdmin,
  };
}

export function useCurrentOrg() {
  const context = useContext(TenantContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useCurrentOrg must be used within TenantProvider');
  }
  return {
    currentOrg: context.currentOrg,
    setCurrentOrg: context.setCurrentOrg,
  };
}

// RequireRole.tsx

import { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { useMembership } from './TenantProvider';

export interface RequireRoleProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  /** Roles that grant access (any match) */
  roles: string[];
  /** Fallback when user lacks required role */
  fallback?: ReactNode;
  /** Also allow platform admins */
  allowPlatformAdmin?: boolean;
}

const ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record<string, number> = {
  guest: 0,
  member: 1,
  admin: 2,
  owner: 3,
  platform_admin: 100,
};

export function RequireRole({
  children,
  roles,
  fallback = null,
  allowPlatformAdmin = true,
}: RequireRoleProps) {
  const { membership, isPlatformAdmin } = useMembership();

  // Platform admin bypass
  if (allowPlatformAdmin && isPlatformAdmin) {
    return <>{children}</>;
  }

  // Check role membership
  const userRole = membership?.role;
  if (!userRole) {
    return <>{fallback}</>;
  }

  // Check if user's role is in allowed list or higher in hierarchy
  const userLevel = ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] ?? 0;
  const hasAccess = roles.some((role) => {
    const requiredLevel = ROLE_HIERARCHY[role] ?? 0;
    return userLevel >= requiredLevel;
  });

  if (!hasAccess) {
    return <>{fallback}</>;
  }

  return <>{children}</>;
}

// Enhanced ProductGraphAdapter with correlation
class ProductGraphAdapter {
  getCorrelationHeaders(): Record<string, string> {
    return {
      'X-Session-ID': this.sessionManager.getSessionId(),
      'X-Request-ID': crypto.randomUUID(),
      'X-Trace-ID': this.getTraceId(),
    };
  }
}

// useAPITracker enhanced
function useAPITracker() {
  const telemetry = useTelemetry();
  const adapter = telemetry.adapter as ProductGraphAdapter;

  return {
    fetch: async (url: string, options?: RequestInit) => {
      const headers = {
        ...options?.headers,
        ...adapter.getCorrelationHeaders(),
      };
      const start = performance.now();
      const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, headers });
      const duration = performance.now() - start;

      telemetry.track({
        type: 'custom',
        name: 'api.response',
        properties: {
          method: options?.method || 'GET',
          path: new URL(url).pathname,
          status_code: response.status,
          duration_ms: Math.round(duration),
        },
      });

      return response;
    },
  };
}

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Modern SaaS applications need comprehensive product analytics that:

  1. Bypass ad blockers - Client-side analytics are increasingly blocked
  2. Unify data sources - Events from frontend, backend, and external systems
  3. Track user journeys - Multi-step flows across pages and sessions
  4. Correlate with backend traces - Link frontend events to backend spans
  5. Forward to multiple providers - Amplitude, Mixpanel, and custom systems

docs.title: US-1: Basic Event Tracking
docs.text:
As a developer, I want to track page views and user actions so that I can understand user behavior.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Track button clicks with component context
  • Events appear in ProductGraph dashboard

docs.title: US-2: Journey Tracking
docs.text:
As a product manager, I want to track multi-step user journeys so that I can measure conversion funnels.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Define journey with steps (e.g., checkout flow)
  • Track step entry, completion, and abandonment
  • Measure time between steps
  • Report conversion rates

docs.title: US-3: State Change Tracking
docs.text:
As a developer, I want to track state changes so that I can debug user sessions.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Track state key, before value, after value
  • Support debouncing for rapid changes
  • Filter sensitive state keys

docs.title: US-4: Backend Correlation
docs.text:
As a DevOps engineer, I want to correlate frontend events with backend traces so that I can debug end-to-end issues.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Propagate session ID to backend via headers
  • Include trace ID in API calls
  • Link ProductGraph events to OpenTelemetry spans

docs.title: US-5: Multi-Provider Analytics
docs.text:
As a data analyst, I want events forwarded to Amplitude and Mixpanel so that I can use existing analysis tools.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Events flow: Frontend → ProductGraph → omnidxi → Amplitude/Mixpanel
  • No frontend changes required
  • Event properties preserved in forwarding

Location: packages/telemetry/src/adapters/productgraph.ts

Responsibilities:

docs.title: Trace ID Propagation
docs.text:
// Frontend: Include session ID in API calls
const headers = {
  'X-Session-ID': sessionId,
  'X-Request-ID': crypto.randomUUID()
};

// Backend: Extract and attach to span
func Middleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    sessionID := r.Header.Get("X-Session-ID")
    requestID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-ID")

    ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), "session_id", sessionID)
    span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
    span.SetAttributes(
      attribute.String("session.id", sessionID),
      attribute.String("request.id", requestID),
    )

    next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
  })
}
